newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures followed Bunds lower early on Thursday and remained stuck in a narrow range, helped by technical support, with little action in the cash market, traders said.

Traders said domestic investors, who were significant buyers of cash bonds at slightly higher levels, were reluctant to take the initiative at the moment and a further move lower was not out of the question.
December and March PIBOR contracts, however, benefited from a stronger franc and weak French household consumption figures which bolstered expectations that rates will be cut again.
French household consumption of manufactured goods fell a surprise 1.5 percent in September as a surge in car purchases failed to offset declines elsewhere.
Traders said the December PIBOR contract kept running into resistance at 96.45, close to the contract high of 96.47 and that the March contract got a boost from one large non-resident order.

Interest rate futures further along the PIBOR strip, however, continued to suffer with Euromark contracts, following statements by Bundesbank officials on Wednesday that there was no reason to cut key German rates.

As a result there was little reaction to the German central bank's decision to leave its repo rate unchanged at three percent after its council meeting on Thursday. Analysts said, however, there was still scope for French rate cuts soon.
The French consumption figures were "very supportive of PIBOR and hopes for a (intervention) rate cut next week," Sonja Gibbs, bond analyst at Nomura International, said.

The franc climbed as high as 3.3752, its highest level since October 8, and up from the day's low of 3.3814 per mark. Traders said the move had been driven by a series of large moves out of Swiss francs into French francs by a U.S. hedge fund.
A trader at a French bank also said French corporates were limiting the decline of the franc much below 3.38 per mark by selling using any weakness to off-load mark positions.

"French corporates sell into any (mark) rally and people are realising there's no upside beyond 3.3820," he said. The move out of the Swiss franc was the only major move boosting the French currency, he said.

The 10-year spread between French and German bond yields remained little changed at minus four compared with minus five on Wednesday. The five-year area of the curve continued to outperform however with the spread narrowing four basis points.
A bond trader at a French bank said further gains in two-year BTANs were unlikely at the moment because of the proximity of two-year yields to overnight money.
Call money was unchanged at 3-1/4 3/8 percent.
